prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val] Extreme · 10 columns + unbreakable values (language en).
Grid: 10 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "ID" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 16px
  col 2: header "SKU" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 136px
  col 3: header "Color" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 40px
  col 4: header "Size" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 31px
  col 5: header "Qty" · longest unbreakable word 26px · one-line width 26px
  col 6: header "Price" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 41px
  col 7: header "Tax" · longest unbreakable word 32px · one-line width 32px
  col 8: header "Total" · longest unbreakable word 47px · one-line width 47px
  col 9: header "Warehouse" · longest unbreakable word 81px · one-line width 122px
  col 10: header "Tracking" · longest unbreakable word 159px · one-line width 159px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 720px. You MAY choose a total wider than 719px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Rendering convention: the screenshot always shows the WHOLE table. Anything beyond the dashed box is not clipped; it is the part a reader reaches by scrolling sideways, so judge both what fits in the box at first sight and the cost of scrolling to the rest.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r1B: widths [38, 110, 61, 52, 47, 62, 53, 68, 102, 180] · table 774×216px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/10 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 54px
Design r1C: widths [38, 157, 61, 52, 47, 62, 53, 68, 102, 180] · table 821×216px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/10 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 101px
Design r2A: widths [38, 95, 61, 52, 47, 62, 53, 68, 143, 180] · table 800×216px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/10 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 80px
Design r2B: widths [38, 157, 61, 52, 47, 62, 53, 68, 143, 180] · table 862×146px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers wrapped 0/10 · tallest cell 1 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 142px
Design r2C: widths [38, 95, 61, 52, 47, 62, 53, 68, 102, 140] · table 719×216px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/10 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 2
Design r3A: widths [38, 95, 61, 52, 47, 62, 53, 68, 102, 180] · table 759×216px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/10 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 39px
Design r3B: widths [38, 95, 61, 52, 47, 62, 53, 68, 102, 161] · table 740×216px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/10 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 2 · OVERFLOWS the box by 20px
Design r3C: widths [38, 115, 61, 52, 47, 62, 53, 68, 102, 180] · table 779×216px · row heights [36, 60, 60, 60] · column headers wrapped 0/10 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 59px

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}
